name: Copenhagen
title: Holidays in Copenhagen
intro: Old-fashioned fairground rides, harbour swims and the home of Lego next door. Here's what Copenhagen is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: Colourful old townhouses and wooden boats reflected in the Nyhavn canal
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May to August has long light evenings, harbour swimming and Tivoli in full swing. Tivoli also opens for Halloween and for Christmas, from mid-November into early January, when the city's Christmas markets are on too. January to March is cold, dark and quiet.

things.name: Tivoli Gardens
things.blurb: A fairy-tale amusement park from 1843, open in summer, at Halloween and at Christmas.

things.name: Tivoli at Christmas
things.blurb: From mid-November to early January, Tivoli fills with lights, Christmas market stalls and the smell of gløgg, Denmark's mulled wine. The rides stay open, and it's at its prettiest after dark, which in December comes at about 4pm.

things.name: Den Blå Planet
things.blurb: Northern Europe's biggest aquarium, with a shark tunnel and sea otters.

things.name: Harbour baths
things.blurb: Swim in clean harbour water at Islands Brygge in summer.

things.name: Canal boat tour
things.blurb: See Nyhavn's coloured houses and the Little Mermaid from the water.

things.name: Experimentarium
things.blurb: A hands-on science centre that keeps all ages busy for hours.

things.name: CopenHill
things.blurb: A dry ski slope and climbing wall on top of a power station.

faqs.question: Is Copenhagen good for a city break?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's small, safe and flat, so you can walk or cycle almost everywhere, and it's great for food, design and harbour swimming. It's easy with children too, with playgrounds everywhere and some of the best family attractions in Europe. Hiring a cargo bike is a fun way to get around.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Three or four nights is plenty for the city. Add a few days if you want to visit Legoland in Billund, about three hours away.

faqs.question: Do you need a visa from the UK?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days in any 180 without a visa. New EU entry checks are being brought in, so check GOV.UK before you travel.

faqs.question: Is Copenhagen expensive?
faqs.answer: Yes, eating out costs more than in the UK. A Copenhagen Card covers transport and most attractions, and up to two children under 12 travel free with each adult.

faqs.question: When is Tivoli Gardens open at Christmas?
faqs.answer: Tivoli's Christmas season usually runs from mid-November to early January. Opening hours and closed days change from year to year, so check the calendar on tivoli.dk before you book.

faqs.question: Is Copenhagen good for a Christmas trip?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tivoli, the Christmas market at Nyhavn and the lights along Strøget make it one of Europe's best Christmas city breaks. It's cold and dark by mid-afternoon, so plan some indoor stops, like Den Blå Planet or a cosy café.
